terms.comment: Of houses, dinners, funerals, games and deeds: grand, splendid, costly. Of a person it means high-minded, or fond of display (Sall. C. 9; Nep. Att. 13); in Plautus, boastful (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: splendid; of a way of living, sumptuous
evidence: Cic. Par. 38: quōrum in vīllā ac domō nihil splendidum fuit praeter ipsōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First bright, shining; then splendid in dress and way of living, and of people distinguished (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: large and imposing; of rank, distinguished
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.139: ampla domus dēdecorī dominō fit, sī est in eā sōlitūdō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Grand as spacious and stately: a house, honours, a funeral; the superlative amplissimus is Cicero’s word for men of the highest rank (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: atque omne ignōtum prō magnificō est
phrases.english: and everything unknown is taken for something grand

phrases.latin: ampla domus dēdecorī dominō fit, sī est in eā sōlitūdō
phrases.english: a grand house is a disgrace to its master if it stands empty
